archetypes.name: Distrustful routine skeptics
archetypes.text: People who say you can't be too careful with others yet still check political information online, and who feel mostly unenthused about politics and democracy while staying pretty happy overall. They report a stalled, below-average family income and see themselves as lower class, but rate the economy as neither good nor bad and keep close ties with relatives. Their unusual mix is strong unease about robots and AI paired with ordinary, mid-level views on science spending and technology, so their worries about automation sit oddly beside their calm, routine outlook on life.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, comfortable-with-tech skeptics
archetypes.text: These people are deeply distrustful of other people and of institutions alike, yet they are not disengaged: they find life exciting and feel their finances are improving. Their cynicism about politics and the economy coexists with optimism about personal circumstances. They are enthusiastic about technology and AI while being openly skeptical that science funding is worthwhile, a combination that runs against the usual pairing of institutional trust with pro-science views.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content loners
archetypes.text: People who report low general trust and skepticism toward institutions and information online, yet feel financially secure and pleased with their own situation. They tend to be disengaged from politics and dissatisfied with democracy while not feeling unhappy in daily life, and they often show mild or strong discomfort with robots and AI taking over human tasks. Their social lives are thin and routine, with infrequent evenings out, and their views on family, technology and science are mixed, with some surprising mismatches between attitudes and everyday habits.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, disengaged, tech-skeptical
archetypes.text: Respondents here combine low trust in people and institutions with a strong habit of checking political information independently, which reads as wary rather than naive. They feel their families are financially worse off yet place themselves in the middle of the income range, and they describe economic conditions and democracy's performance negatively while staying politically uninterested. Their life outlook is flat, with dull routines but moderate social contact. Unusually, they strongly reject technology's benefits yet are not anxious about AI, and they want more public spending on science. Their attitudes cut across usual partisan or ideological lines, so they resist easy categorization.
